title: Separating Fact from Fiction: AI Does Not Set Prices at McDonald’s

reading.body:
This incident is a dispute over what a deployed system does, not a documented account of what it did. The only substantive claim in the record is a class action complaint alleging that AI was used in menu pricing, and the only substantive response is the company's own published denial that AI sets its prices. The underlying complaint document could not be read, so the specific mechanism alleged, the pricing conduct at issue, and the time period involved are not established here.

The failure mode, to the extent the record supports one, is an allegation of automated price coordination, which is a claim about how a system was used rather than a demonstrated defect in a model. Nothing in the available material shows that any AI system made or influenced a pricing decision, and nothing shows the conditions under which such a system would have been deployed. Catching conduct of this kind would require visibility into how pricing inputs are generated and combined, which is exactly the kind of detail the unreadable complaint would have supplied.

A filed complaint is an allegation, not a finding, and a company's public denial is a statement of position, not an adjudicated fact. No court has ruled on the claim in the material given, and no outcome is reported.
